account: Today my ordinary mayoral duties continue: the mill inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at one, tea with my neighbour at three, and office time at half past four. The unusual business is an evening civic presentation in the town hall great hall, from six to half past six. The innkeeper is organising it with local tradespeople, and the secretary has entered my approval in a signed appointment supplement and relayed it to the innkeeper. They have repeatedly stressed that I should arrive precisely at six, not earlier. I heard the secretary say she would keep the presentation's contents private. The stated subject is appreciation of municipal public service. I suspect they are arranging a surprise appreciation gathering, probably for me, though I have not seen the preparations or established exactly what they intend. Yesterday I saw the builder give the baker planks and a lantern; that might relate to preparations, but I do not know. My neighbour has also been asking people about riverside improvements and will report at tea. That seems consistent with ordinary town business rather than necessarily part of the presentation. The ferry operator suggested lights at both landings and clearly marked waiting areas away from the water, which I asked the secretary to note. Nothing I have actually heard establishes any sinister scheme; the private arrangements seem most likely intended to preserve the presentation's surprise.
